findings.title: Use the booking organizer's credentials for calendar updates
findings.body: The handler permits attendees and team administrators to add guests, but constructs EventManager with the caller and the caller's credentials. When the caller is not the organizer, these credentials cannot update the organizer's existing calendar event; they may also target the caller's calendar instead. Load the booking owner's credentials and initialize EventManager for that owner so that adding guests actually updates the calendar event associated with the booking.

findings.title: Authorize team administrators or owners, not both
findings.body: isTeamAdminOrOwner combines isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner with &&. A team administrator who is not the owner therefore fails this check and receives FORBIDDEN unless they are also the organizer or an attendee. Use an OR check to grant the intended access to either team role.

findings.title: Deduplicate guests on the server before inserting attendees
findings.body: uniqueGuests only removes addresses already present in the booking; it does not remove repeated addresses within the request. The server schema accepts duplicate strings, so a direct mutation with the same new email twice passes validation and sends both entries to createMany, producing duplicate attendees or an insertion failure if a database constraint rejects them. The uniqueness refinement in the dialog does not protect the API. Enforce uniqueness in the server schema or deduplicate before insertion.

findings.title: Normalize guest addresses when applying the blacklist
findings.body: BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS is converted to lowercase, but each submitted guest is compared without normalization. A blacklisted address submitted with uppercase characters passes the email schema and bypasses the blacklist, allowing an invitation to the blocked mailbox. Normalize submitted addresses before the blacklist comparison and use the same normalization for duplicate detection.

findings.title: Respect disabled standard-email settings when adding guests
findings.body: sendAddGuestsEmails unconditionally sends organizer and attendee emails and does not accept event-type metadata. Other booking notification functions in this file honor disableStandardEmails.all.host and disableStandardEmails.all.attendee. Adding guests consequently sends standard notifications even for event types whose owners explicitly disabled them, potentially duplicating custom workflow notifications. Pass the event-type metadata from the handler and apply the existing host and attendee suppression checks.

findings.title: Provide recovery when calendar synchronization fails after insertion
findings.body: New attendees are committed to the database before updateCalendarAttendees is awaited. If calendar synchronization throws, the mutation returns an error even though the guests were added, and notification emails are never attempted. Retrying the same request then filters out those guests and returns BAD_REQUEST, so the normal retry path cannot repair the calendar or deliver their invitations. Make synchronization retryable for already-added guests or otherwise handle partial completion explicitly rather than leaving the booking permanently out of sync after an error.
